slides.title: WX-11: retain the coarser distribution
slides.subtitle: {{PRJ0110:project_id}} | {{PRJ0110:lims_id}} | Wexanthel Medicines | Miguel Serrano | 07/24/2018 | FINAL final | Durnesswick Laboratories Inc

slides.title: Recommendation retained
bullets: Wexanthel Medicines retained the coarser particle-size distribution.
The micronised pilot lot formed a compact cake.
Smaller particles did not give the preferred handling behavior.
slides.notes: FINAL final working revision: handoff wording now emphasizes recovery after standing rather than initial appearance.

slides.title: Vehicle ladder: physical behavior beside capacity
Equilibrium capacity is only part of the choice
slides.notes: Target loading 10 mg/mL. This chart does not measure dilution behavior or particle-size distribution.

slides.title: Work package history
bullets: Started 06/01/2018; interim discussion 06/27/2018; completed 07/24/2018.
Miguel Serrano prepared the comparison under Julia Carver’s development lead.
Lena Patel supported the practical dosing handoff.

slides.title: Particle-size comparison: qualitative conclusion
bullets: Coarser pilot lot retained for dosing.
Recoverability after settling is more useful than a fine appearance alone.
bullets_right: Micronised pilot lot settled into a compact cake.
The handling penalty outweighed the expected benefit of size reduction.
slides.notes: No D10, D50 or D90 measurements in µm are supplied. The solubility chart is not a particle-size plot.

slides.title: Redispersion is a use condition
bullets: Compare the settled preparation before and after the defined mixing step.
Note base adhesion and hard sediment that remains.
Uniform appearance during active mixing does not establish recovery after standing.

slides.title: Keep vehicle and size as separate variables
bullets: The ladder distinguishes redispersible preparations from caking preparations.
The particle-size follow-up independently identified the micronised compact cake.
Do not assign that failure to a ladder row without the linked recipe card.

rows: Retain coarser distribution; no micronised substitution
Report future measured distributions in µm
Repeat recovery assessment before extending use

slides.title: Complete decision; further process work
bullets: The client’s choice of coarser material is complete.
The compact cake explains the rejection of micronisation.
bullets_right: This deck sets no numerical size specification.
Transfer-scale preparation and storage claims need supporting observations.

slides.title: Handoff to Lena Patel
bullets: Carry material condition and resuspension instructions together.
Retain both pilot-lot observations so the rejected route remains understandable.
Agree container geometry and mixing method before larger preparation.

slides.title: Final position / working revision retained
bullets: Coarser material retained; micronisation is not the default next step.
Future changes should address recovery, concentration and manufacturability together.
FINAL final wording: “redispersible after standing” replaces “fine suspension” in the handoff.
slides.notes: Presentation wording revised; the scientific choice is unchanged.
